# Awesome-Selfhosted

[![Awesome](_static/awesome.png)](https://github.com/sindresorhus/awesome) [![](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted-data/actions/workflows/check-dead-links.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted-data/issues/1) [![](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted-data/actions/workflows/check-unmaintained-projects.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted-data/issues/1) [![](https://img.shields.io/liberapay/goal/awesome-selfhosted?logo=liberapay)](https://liberapay.com/awesome-selfhosted/)

Self-hosting is the practice of hosting and managing applications on your own server(s) instead of consuming from [SaaSS](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/who-does-that-server-really-serve.html) providers.

This is a list of [Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_software) Software [network services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_service) and [web applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application) which can be hosted on your own server(s). Non-Free software is listed on the [Non-Free](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted/blob/master/non-free.md) page.

**[HTML version](https://awesome-selfhosted.net/) (recommended)**, [Markdown version](https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted) (legacy).

See [Contributing](#contributing).

--------------------

## Software

### Analytics

**[`^        back to top        ^`](#awesome-selfhosted)**

[Analytics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytics) is the systematic computational analysis of data or statistics. It is used for the discovery, interpretation, and communication of meaningful patterns in data.

_Related: [Database Management](#database-management), [Personal Dashboards](#personal-dashboards)_

- [ANALOG](https://github.com/orangecoloured/analog) - A minimal analytics tool. Tracks events in a span of 10-30 days. `MIT` `Nodejs/Docker`
- [Aptabase](https://aptabase.com/) - Privacy first and simple analytics for mobile and desktop apps. ([Source Code](https://github.com/aptabase/aptabase)) `AGPL-3.0` `Docker`
- [AWStats](http://www.awstats.org/) - Generate statistics from web, streaming, ftp or mail server logfiles. ([Demo](https://www.awstats.org/#DEMO), [Source Code](https://github.com/eldy/awstats)) `GPL-3.0` `Perl`
- [Countly Community Edition](https://count.ly) - Real time mobile and web analytics, crash reporting and push notifications platform. ([Source Code](https://github.com/Countly/countly-server)) `AGPL-3.0` `Nodejs/Docker`
- [d8a.tech](https://d8a.tech) - A data collection service that works with your existing Google Analytics setup to capture user activity and send it straight to your own private database. ([Demo](https://lookerstudio.google.com/u/0/reporting/0e4102b6-c38b-4f55-aa25-c1fe91d1c1e9), [Source Code](https://github.com/d8a-tech/d8a)) `MIT` `Go/Docker`
- [Daily Stars Explorer](https://emanuelef.github.io/daily-stars-explorer) `⚠` - Track GitHub repo trends with daily star insights to see growth and community interest over time. ([Demo](https://emanuelef.github.io/daily-stars-explorer), [Source Code](https://github.com/emanuelef/daily-stars-explorer)) `MIT` `Go/Nodejs/Docker`
- [Druid](https://druid.apache.org) - Distributed, column-oriented, real-time analytics data store. ([Source Code](https://github.com/apache/druid)) `Apache-2.0` `Java/Docker`
- [EDA](https://github.com/jortilles/EDA) - Web application for data analysis and visualization. `AGPL-3.0` `Nodejs/Docker`
- [GoAccess](http://goaccess.io/) - Real-time web log analyzer and interactive viewer that runs in a terminal. ([Source Code](https://github.com/allinurl/goaccess)) `GPL-2.0` `C`
- [GoatCounter](https://www.goatcounter.com) - Easy web statistics without tracking of personal data. ([Source Code](https://github.com/arp242/goatcounter)) `EUPL-1.2` `Go`
- [HitKeep](https://hitkeep.com/) - Privacy-first web analytics with goals, funnels, ecommerce tracking, and team management in a single binary with embedded DuckDB (alternative to Google Analytics, Plausible, Umami). ([Source Code](https://github.com/pascalebeier/hitkeep)) `MIT` `Go/Docker`
- [Litlyx](https://litlyx.com) - All-in-one Analytics Solution. Setup in 30 seconds. Display all your data on an AI-powered dashboard. Fully self-hostable and GDPR compliant. ([Source Code](https://github.com/Litlyx/litlyx)) `Apache-2.0` `Docker`
- [Liwan](https://liwan.dev/) - Privacy-first web analytics. ([Demo](https://demo.liwan.dev/p/liwan.dev), [Source Code](https://github.com/explodingcamera/liwan)) `Apache-2.0` `Rust/Docker`
- [Matomo](https://matomo.org/) - Web analytics that protects your data and your customers' privacy (alternative to Google Analytics). ([Source Code](https://github.com/matomo-org/matomo)) `GPL-3.0` `PHP`
- [Medama Analytics](https://oss.medama.io) - Privacy-first website analytics. Tiny, simple, and cookie-free. ([Demo](https://demo.medama.io), [Source Code](https://github.com/medama-io/medama)) `Apache-2.0/MIT` `Docker/Go`
- [Metabase](https://metabase.com/) - Easy way for everyone in your company to ask questions and learn from data. ([Source Code](https://github.com/metabase/metabase)) `AGPL-3.0` `Java/Docker`
- [Middleware](https://middlewarehq.com/) - Tool designed to help engineering leaders measure and analyze the effectiveness of their teams using the DORA metrics. ([Source Code](https://github.com/middlewarehq/middleware)) `Apache-2.0` `Docker/Python/Nodejs`
- [Mixpost](https://mixpost.app/) - Social media management software to easily create, schedule, publish, and manage social media content in one place (alternative to Hootsuite and Buffer). ([Source Code](https://github.com/inovector/MixpostApp)) `MIT` `PHP/Docker`

scout.summary: The repository is a fork of the well-known 'awesome-selfhosted' list, presenting a curated collection of free and self-hostable web applications and services. It emphasizes software freedom, privacy, and alternatives to SaaSS (Software as a Service), with clear categorization and licensing information.
highlights: Clearly defines self-hosting as an alternative to SaaSS, aligning with Free Software philosophy [ID:E-RD-002].
Exclusively lists Free Software in the main README, segregating Non-Free options into a separate file [ID:E-RD-003].
Provides structured, categorized listings (e.g., Analytics, Backup, Email) with project links, licenses, and tech stacks [ID:E-RD-005, E-RD-008].
Includes active maintenance indicators like CI badges for dead link and unmaintained project checks [ID:E-RD-001].
Offers both HTML (recommended) and Markdown versions for accessibility and usability [ID:E-RD-004].
risks: A closed issue reports that 'every link tried to open in this repo' may be broken or misrouted, suggesting potential navigation or redirection problems [ID:E-IS-001].

The repository appears to be a fork or mirror (based on content referencing awesome-selfhosted.net and original org), but lacks clear attribution or sync status, risking staleness or confusion [ID:E-RD-001, E-RD-004].

inventor.summary: The repository functions as a comprehensive, categorized directory of self-hostable free software, enabling users to discover and deploy privacy-respecting alternatives to SaaSS. It invents no new software but curates and structures existing tools into a navigable knowledge resource with licensing and deployment metadata.
highlights: Invents a structured taxonomy for self-hosted applications across domains like analytics, email, backup, and automation, facilitating discovery and comparison [ID:E-RD-005].
Introduces a dual-format delivery system (HTML and Markdown) to optimize user experience and accessibility [ID:E-RD-004].
Embeds metadata directly in listings—such as license type, tech stack, and source code links—enabling informed deployment decisions [ID:E-RD-008].
Segregates Non-Free software into a dedicated file, reinforcing a principled stance on software freedom within the curation framework [ID:E-RD-003].
risks: The curated list may suffer from link rot or misrouting, as indicated by a closed issue reporting broken navigation, which undermines its utility as a reliable directory [ID:E-IS-001].

As a likely fork or mirror of the upstream 'awesome-selfhosted' project, it lacks explicit versioning or sync indicators, risking outdated or inconsistent content without clear provenance [ID:E-RD-001, E-RD-004].

engineer.summary: The repository is a curated list of free, self-hostable software organized into functional categories with metadata like licenses and tech stacks. It functions as a reference directory rather than a deployable application, relying on external projects for actual implementation.
highlights: Structured categorization (e.g., Analytics, Email, Backup) enables efficient discovery of self-hosted alternatives [ID:E-RD-005].
Each listed project includes license type and runtime environment (e.g., `MIT` `Nodejs/Docker`), aiding deployment feasibility assessment [ID:E-RD-008].
Clear separation of Free vs. Non-Free software reinforces adherence to Free Software principles [ID:E-RD-003].
CI badges indicate automated checks for dead links and unmaintained projects, suggesting active curation [ID:E-RD-001].
risks: A closed issue reports broken or misrouted links across the repository, which could hinder usability and trust in the directory [ID:E-IS-001].
The repo appears to be a fork or mirror of the upstream 'awesome-selfhosted' project but lacks clear sync status or attribution, risking stale or inconsistent content [ID:E-RD-001, E-RD-004].

skeptic.summary: The repository presents itself as a principled, well-maintained directory of free self-hosted software, but critical issues around link integrity, provenance, and actual maintenance cast doubt on its reliability and independence.
highlights: Claims active maintenance via CI badges for dead links and unmaintained projects [ID:E-RD-001], yet a closed issue reports systemic link failures [ID:E-IS-001], suggesting checks may be ineffective or ignored.

Presents a clean separation of Free and Non-Free software [ID:E-RD-003], but the list appears to be a repackaged fork of upstream 'awesome-selfhosted' without clear attribution or sync status [ID:E-RD-004].
Recommends an external HTML version as primary [ID:E-RD-004], implying this GitHub repo is secondary or legacy—undermining claims of it being a canonical or actively curated source.
risks: Despite CI badges suggesting automated quality control [ID:E-RD-001], a user-reported issue confirms widespread broken links [ID:E-IS-001], indicating either failed automation or lack of follow-up—eroding trust in curation quality.

The repository mirrors content from awesome-selfhosted.net and the original organization [ID:E-RD-001, E-RD-004] but provides no transparency about update frequency, divergence, or ownership, raising concerns about staleness and misrepresentation.
No releases, minimal forks, and only one (closed) issue suggest low community engagement or independent maintenance, contradicting the appearance of an active, standalone project.
